title: Honda Brings Hotter Civic Type R, Hybrid Trophy Truck, and Performance Parts to SEMA 2026

body_markdown:
Honda will highlight its racing past, present, and future at the Specialty Equipment Market’s annual trade show in Las Vegas (November 3–6). Honda will travel to Las Vegas to display a dozen performance cars, including an evolution of[the Civic Type R](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/honda-sharpens-civic-type-r-for-2027/) that’s on its way to production and that will be sold on the U.S. market.


That car is the big news. It’s called[the Civic Type R HRC Concept](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/hotter-honda-civic-type-r-inbound/) and was developed by[the Honda Racing Corporation division](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/hello-hrc-hondas-performance-division-is-heating-up/) that engineers the cars Honda races globally. It’s not technically new—it was unveiled at the 2026 Tokyo Auto Salon—but this is the first time it will be shown in the United States. Honda isn’t merely teasing us: The manufacturer confirmed that the model will spawn a production model bound for the U.S. Honda hasn’t released specifications, and there’s no word on when the Civic Type R HRC Concept will reach showrooms, but we could learn more at SEMA. And while it was developed by race car engineers, the hotter Type R is expected to be street-legal.


Honda


Honda


Other highlights from Honda’s SEMA 2026 display include the new Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck. It is the first hybrid-powered Trophy Truck to race in the SCORE World Desert Championship, and Honda Racing Corporation (HRC), together with Mason Motorsports, is hoping to win first overall in the legendary Baja 1000 alongside Menzies Motorsports. Entering a hybrid into a race dominated by nine-liter V-8s might sound like wishful thinking, but producing power is not a problem: The system is built around a 2.4-liter twin-turbocharged V-6 supplemented by an 800V hybrid architecture and delivers a peak output of 1300 horsepower.


Honda


One of the three[Passport TrailSport](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2022-honda-passport-trailsport-review-semblance-and-substance/) –based chase vehicles built to support the Passport Baja Spec will be shown at SEMA as well. While it looks like something you could find in a showroom, it has been modified for a Borla exhaust system, HRC dampers, and HRC forged-aluminum wheels wrapped in meaty tires.


Hasport Prelude Club Racer:


Honda


Moving back to the pavement, the new Hasport Prelude Club Race will break cover in Las Vegas. It was designed to race in time-attack track events, and it’s powered by a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine linked to a six-speed manual transmission. Hasport, for those who aren’t familiar, is the largest manufacturer of engine-swap components for Honda and Acura.


The 2026 Aston Martin AMR26 Formula 1 car will be at SEMA as well. Honda and Aston Martin are independent of each other, but the AMR26 uses the Honda RA626H power unit that’s built around a 1.6-liter turbocharged V-6. Several other race cars will be displayed at the show, including the Indy car that won the 2026 Indy 500 and the electrified 2026 Acura ARX-06 GTP Prototype endurance racer.


If you’re after an ambitious winter project, the 2009 Acura ARX-02a Patrón driven by David Brabham, Scott Sharp, and Dario Franchitti in the LMP1 category of the American Le Mans Series needs a new home. Honda notes that it needs to be restored. You’ll be able to check it out at the Honda Racing Corporation booth, though don’t expect the brand to offer a test drive. If you’d rather not dive into a restoration, Honda is also selling the recently restored 2017 NSX GT3 in its “Lady Liberty” livery.


Beyond race cars, Honda Racing Corporation will launch a line of performance parts for on- and off-road models at SEMA 2026. The catalog will initially include exhaust systems, lightweight forged wheels, and a short-throw shifter. The parts were designed to fit a wide range of Honda and Acura models, including the Civic Type R,[the Integra Type S](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/for-me-acuras-integra-type-s-makes-the-case-for-embracing-evolution/) , and the Passport TrailSport. Some of the company’s upcoming performance parts, such as adjustable coilovers and a Brembo big-brake kit, will be at the show as well.

Finally, show-goers will be able to purchase merchandise and memorabilia from Honda Racing Corporation. We’re not just talking about a baseball hat: Honda will give attendees the opportunity to buy piston and connecting rod assemblies, camshafts, valves, and a camshaft cover from a race-used RA100E V-10 Formula 1 engine. Each part will be sold with a certificate of authenticity.


SEMA 2026 will take place from November 3 to 6 at the Las Vegas Convention Center, and Hagerty ** will be on-location to bring you live updates from the event. Stay tuned!
